narrative.overview:
This is a system for managing living things — models, keys, credits, usage — behind clean glass panels. The interface is organized like a greenhouse: transparent, structured, and alive. Every surface is a window into a system that grows and changes. The green accent isn't decoration; it's health, status, connection.

The system rejects noise. No gradient heroes, no card grids with icon-heading-paragraph repeating endlessly, no eyebrow text above every section. Information density is welcome when it serves the task; cognitive overload is not. Every screen answers one question.

Both light and dark themes are first-class. Neither is a default or an afterthought. The light theme is a clean workbench; the dark theme is a control room.
keyCharacteristics: Functional color — emerald communicates state, not decoration. Appears on ≤10% of any screen.
Tonal neutrality — achromatic grays carry all structural weight. No warm or cool tint.
Warm approachability — rounded, tactile, responsive components. Pill buttons, soft corners.
Breathing room — generous spacing between sections, tight spacing within components.

rules.name: The 10% Rule
rules.body: The primary accent appears on ≤10% of any given screen. Its rarity is the point. If every button is green, no button is green.

rules.name: The Zero-Chroma Rule
rules.body: All neutrals — backgrounds, cards, borders, muted text, dividers — are achromatic (chroma = 0). No warm gray, no cool gray. Tinted neutrals are prohibited.

rules.name: The Functional Color Rule
rules.body: Color communicates state, not decoration. Green means active/connected/valid/success. Red means error/danger/destructive. No color on a surface that doesn't carry meaning.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Inter carries every text element in the product. No display font, no serif pairing, no secondary sans. Geist Mono is the only exception for code-adjacent contexts.

rules.name: The Fixed-Scale Rule
rules.body: Type sizes are fixed rem values, not fluid clamp scales. The sole exception is the display heading on the landing page.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No component ships with a shadow in its resting state. Shadows are earned through interaction.

rules.name: The Ambient-Not-Dramatic Rule
rules.body: Shadows are soft, low-opacity, and large-blur. Hard-edged or high-contrast shadows are prohibited.

dos: Use Fresh Emerald sparingly — primary buttons, active states, success indicators. The 10% Rule applies.
Use achromatic neutrals for all structural surfaces.
Make both themes feel intentional. Light is a workbench; dark is a control room.
Use pill radii on buttons. Every button is fully rounded.
Use 150ms ease-out transitions on interactive state changes.
Show a number before a chart.
Use skeleton states for loading, not spinners.
Keep shadows ambient and subtle. Flat by default; lift on interaction.
Use Geist Mono only for code, API keys, and terminal output.
donts: Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text with a gradient).
Don't use side-stripe borders (border-left/right > 1px as colored accent).
Don't use glassmorphism as a default.
Don't put tiny uppercase tracked eyebrows above every section.
Don't use numbered section markers (01/02/03) as default scaffolding.
Don't use identical card grids — same-sized cards with icon + heading + text.
Don't use the hero-metric template — big number, small label, stats, gradient accent.
Don't use overly complex dashboards with 15 charts and 3 sidebars.
Don't use dark-only or dev-tool cliché aesthetics.
Don't use border-radius: 32px+ on cards or sections.
Don't use tinted neutrals. Achromatic means chroma = 0.
Don't use a display font for UI labels, buttons, or data.
Don't use bounce or elastic easing.
